a1.name: Boro Indigo Mends
a1.prompt: A man sits on the cold pavement of the Thames embankment in London at night, his back to the stone river wall, a small green tent beside him and the lit dome of St Paul's behind across the water. His whole head and face are covered by a closed hood pieced from faded indigo cotton and hemp patches in a dozen blues, patched over and over, held by rows of white running stitches in straight geometric lines, frayed edges lifting. Where the face would be is unbroken patched cloth, with no eye holes, no mouth and no openings. A thick white cotton ring sewn with dense white cross-stitches circles the face, and high inside it, on the right-hand side of the picture at about two o'clock, sits a small cut patch of faded red cotton in a triangle. He wears a big ex-army field jacket over a navy hoodie, jumpers at the cuffs, mismatched full wool gloves, a matted grey scarf tucked round the neck, a rolled sleeping bag at his side. Mid-verse, one gloved hand pressed flat on his chest, the other palm open toward the lens, head tilted forward. Waist-up, eye level, lit by a sodium streetlamp, high-ISO grain.
a1.why: A mask mended for decades carries poverty and care at once, so his dignity is in the stitches.

a2.name: Foil Blanket Wrap
a2.prompt: Under a concrete motorway flyover in west London at night, a man raps straight into a wide lens, close and waist-up, graffiti on the pillars and small tents behind, a fire burning in an oil drum beside him. His whole head and face are wrapped tight in a crinkled silver-and-gold emergency foil blanket, fastened with strips of matte black gaffer tape; the face is one unbroken crumpled surface with no eye holes, no mouth and no openings. A wide band of white cloth tape is wound in a ring round the face, and high inside it, on the right-hand side of the picture at about two o'clock, is a small triangle cut from red electrical tape, its edges slightly lifting. He wears a rain-dark parka over a grey hoodie, black work gloves covering every finger, the foil tucked into a wound brown scarf. He jabs a pointed gloved finger at the lens, foreshortened, as the fire's orange light flares in hard, broken highlights across the creases. Handheld, low angle, crushed blacks, high-ISO noise.
a2.why: The cheapest armour against a night outside, and firelight on crinkled foil looks like no other frame.
